item: R13: subset test for violated segments that gained rows after sealing; offline insertion experiment

rule.existing: violation with delta_n <= 0 (or segment vanished): attributable; delta_n > 0: ambiguous
rule.subset_test: delta_n = k > 0: search every anchored-size subsequence of the segment's current rows (time order, ties by key) for one whose hash chain equals the anchored root; none: a sealed row was edited or deleted (attributable); one: the sealed rows are intact and the complement is the added rows; k > 8 or C(N+k,k) above the budget without a late-row witness: ambiguous
rule.late_row_hypothesis: the k+1 candidates dropping the j newest state rows and k-j newest event rows (largest primary keys); a match is an exact witness of intact sealed rows

part_b.what: closure-scheme runs; synthetic state rows (copy of the nearest state row, fresh state_id, time columns moved to a timestamp drawn uniformly inside the target second) inserted into a copy of the saved recorder; B1: one-second segments of trials the existing rule attributes; B2: untouched anchored one-second segments whose root reproduces

variants.one_row: B1 one row; B2 one row
variants.count_above_anchored: B1 1 - delta_n rows (the fewest that make the count exceed the anchored count); B2 k = 2..8 rows, cycling
variants.k_8: B1 8 - delta_n rows, so the segment holds 8 rows more than anchored
variants.count_above_anchored_old_keys: as count_above_anchored for B1 and one row for B2, but each inserted row takes a state_id below the table's smallest, older than every sealed row: the exact search must find it, the late-row hypothesis cannot

caveats: e_d_auth: the verifier's own snapshot is not in the set; the later recorder copy hp_d2/live is used, as verify_all.py does, so its late-row breakdown is not the run-time one.
e_c_write_time and e_d_other_principal_real have no saved verifier snapshot; their late-row floor failures are listed from file and not re-scored.
The subset test rests on SHA-256 collision resistance: a reproduced chain is taken to mean the same node hashes in the same order.
The late-row hypothesis assumes the recorder assigns primary keys in commit order (SQLite rowid max+1); it is reported beside the exhaustive verdict, which does not assume it.
Part B inserts rows offline into copies; no live adversary inserted rows.
